findings.summary: I0, I1, W0, and D0 all passed the exact ORT/vGPU oracle. W0 and D0 also passed hash-bound application replay and the frozen post-destroy error-handler lifecycle regression on the physical AMD Vulkan adapter.

D0 did not produce a lifecycle outcome unavailable from W0. Both governed lanes passed the same oracle, post-destroy regression, and replay identity, so this diagnostic assigns no unique lifecycle-control value to DoeRuntime.

limitations: Three clean processes per lane remain diagnostic and do not satisfy the promotion reliability floor.
The selected failure injection covers the retained post-destroy error-handler regression, not device loss, concurrency, leak growth, or the full lifecycle surface.
Clean-process durations are diagnostic and do not constitute matched selected-operation performance evidence.
P0 is conditional for lifecycle control and was not required because no bounded incumbent correction claim was adjudicated.
The result does not justify making vGPU a DoeRuntime release blocker.

performance.reason: The diagnostic records clean-process durations but does not run the frozen selected-operation performance protocol.

receiptOverhead.reason: Matched traced and untraced receipt-overhead samples were not collected.

I0.summary: The unchanged application resolved its ordinary workspace WebGPU provider and passed three clean oracle runs.

I1.summary: The explicitly pinned Dawn module passed three clean oracle runs.

W0.summary: Pinned Dawn plus governed identity, lifecycle injection, receipt, and replay passed.

D0.summary: DoeRuntime under the identical governed contract passed.

P0.summary: The lifecycle-control hypothesis did not require an independent-correction patch control.

materialOutcome.summary: D0 did not materially exceed W0 on the frozen lifecycle outcome; both passed every exercised obligation.

costAcceptance.summary: No unique application benefit was measured to repay DoeRuntime's additional source, compatibility, security, packaging, and support obligations.

installation.summary: The diagnostic reused a prepared workspace and provider-loader substitution rather than a production installation path.

supportHardware.summary: The preparation receipt and governed provider probes bind execution to the physical Radeon 8060S RADV adapter.

concurrency.summary: The diagnostic uses sequential clean processes.

teardown.summary: Every workload and replay passed the existing vGPU teardown assertions and the post-destroy handler regression.

stress.summary: Promotion-scale stress and device-loss injection were not run.

memory.summary: Peak process memory was recorded, but bounded-growth leak testing was not run.

receipts.summary: The reviewed raw matrix, summary, and per-provider replay receipts are hash-bound.

replay.summary: W0 and D0 each reproduced the exact frozen application evidence hash from a persisted replay receipt.

performance.summary: No selected-operation performance decision was run.

ownership.summary: The matrix is complete, but D0 supplies no measured lifecycle advantage over W0.

release.summary: vGPU remains a diagnostic integration and is not a DoeRuntime release blocker.
